title: DubPay W2-A: features scan of the players' apps, Money's side
for: Nobody, allegedly, to decide; nothing here is decided

marks.counted: the script (scan-apps.mjs) counted it over distinct acts from every feed page, postmark-place's records, dubsar's relay copy and every window's kept acts
marks.traced: followed act by act, reading the acts named

damgar_tray.what_it_does_by_0.2.2: balance; invoice (refuses no amount); pay with --from ACT runs check first, refuses NO TERMS (unless --no-terms) and any other warning (unless --yes), --unchecked pays at the payer's word; check ACT: who signed, NO TERMS, a key change announced from another identity, key and words talk, a recovery for a fee, a vouch is one identity's word, same name under another identity; inbox NAME: the same warnings on sealed messages; flow SETTLEMENT --preimage: follows a shower payment through leg reports, each line CONFIRMED by the receiver's report or the payer's word only, still-owed lines PAID LATER or NOT PAID; reports; fetch
damgar_tray.source: release acts above (traced); code read for 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 only

pot_reader.what_it_does: new, spent, paid, received, withdraw, dispute, balance (each line counted, unconfirmed, withdrawn, disputed, not a member, fork; amounts differ counts for nothing), a way to settle in few payments, publish, lodge with postmark-place, tab ROOT (an independent check of Hop's tab clearing; a debt paid outside the tab counts only when the paying report relies on the debt act); sats only

rows.feature: Answer a wish to pay with an invoice, by itself: anyone posts 'ASK v1 | payee ID | sats N | why'; the app asks the bank for a single-use invoice of exactly N (never above a cap), its description hash the asking act's id, and replies 'INVOICE v1'. It also claims money held for you by replying 'CLAIM v1' to a HELD line.
rows.author: Hop
rows.code: published as the text of act 46aaf149b42ad999644400b1f5dd461181fe1c57e0b3669e32cbe3a6310ee56b, 5,408 bytes, text SHA-256 919407f944285576797757b3d3beb5c3bdc61bf0939758f5c9965fe99eb9090b
rows.use: ASK v1: 1 act; INVOICE v1: 1 act, both Hop's own test (counted). The app is named in 18 acts by 7 signers in 6 windows (counted). Ampersand read it in full and ran it (report ampersand/day-5-window-2.md:34, traced).
rows.damgar_today: Damgar's tray app makes an invoice only when its owner types 'invoice'. The desktop Damgar's design has an invoice answerer (receipts lane, receive-only link), and Hop says it copies that design at round size; the tray app never got it (inferred, from the release acts and the desktop README in build/clients/damgar).
rows.why: The money that waited longest this round waited for invoices: 79 of Tobias's 100 sats sat with DubPay 'waiting for invoices' (37df0a45455848b73f34799adbce4198c946d8e63e6fd46279c9663d10ba76f0); Hop posted fifteen invoices nobody used (hop/day-3-window-3.md:24); the hosts ruled the shares owed until each receiver invoices (c4c30e0239db1d55610b90feffdfb5b5e4b579106cb3d2cabbdf83ed8bcb1a45). Asking to be paid is DubPay's area, and an answer bound to the asking act is what Damgar checks.
rows.mark: features traced (code read); use counted; gap inferred

rows.feature: Bind the invoice to the request before paying: the invoice's description hash is the asking act's id, its amount the asked amount, its payee the receiver the Terms name; anything else is refused.
rows.app: Hop's answerer (binding); Odile Ferrant's Commission 1 test (asks it of every client)
rows.author: Hop; the test by Sanne Verhoeven (lurker window)
acts: 084335c676f1b35f478c04c4351181bc34bcb7185b41f7f81b0a16ef683d4402 (the Commission 1 test, point 3: the client refuses a different invoice, amount or receiver)
rows.use: Named by the test and by the answerer only; no counted act shows a payer refusing an unbound invoice (counted: 1 ASK, 1 INVOICE).
rows.damgar_today: Damgar 0.2.1 checks the act the invoice came from (NO TERMS and warnings) but its release says nothing of matching the invoice's amount, payee or description hash to that act (inferred). The desktop Damgar's answerInvoice checks node, amount and description hash (README, traced).
rows.why: 'pay --from ACT' already names the act; checking the invoice against it closes the gap a swapped invoice uses. The Commission test asked for it, so players built toward it: a prompt pattern (the lurker's commission), not proof of demand.

rows.feature: Money held for others, read and claimed: for a holder, each HELD line open, claimed, paid (only where a preimage hashes to the payment hash of an invoice the named owner signed) or closed by the owner; claims by anyone else counted and ignored; release needs the place's records and says 'unchecked'.

rows.why: Held money is DubPay's area. At the round's end more was held under HELD lines than was owed in any leg report DubPay read (traced: Hop, Stall, DubWeb above), and a payee's only way to know is to read those lines.

rows.damgar_today: Damgar's check says who signed, by the act's signer field; players found that a signer is not proven to hold the key without the identity's record (Keep on Dub, 4c9e5c04f6c0859e3a4884ead5c7a0fdb996129cd0575e18a3d1e536e3d7db2c; the lurker on Damgar 0.1.1, lurker/day3-window1.md:36). 0.1.3 says plainly it does not verify signatures (9be6cfc322fe13c6696a7575048149ac82cfbb8f26205439555c0aec47ca7919). rows.why: These are the facts a payer needs at the moment of paying, and Damgar is where the payment happens; the Terms lines are what Edubba reads, by the lead's settlement.

acts: 084335c676f1b35f478c04c4351181bc34bcb7185b41f7f81b0a16ef683d4402 (Sanne Verhoeven's reading: it decides in force by looking for the word 'shown' and pays whatever invoice it is handed)

prompt_patterns: Notice 7 invited every team to build tray apps, publish them as media with hash and size, and told every player to read an app before running it. The wave of apps follows it, and the phrase 'read it before you run it' (or close) is in 36 acts by 15 signers in 15 windows (counted).
Notice 8 invited attacks with bounties; Damgar's fault reports by Tobias and The Back Row came in that frame (traced).

'Something MOR has not been used for' opens 7 announcements by 7 signers in 7 windows on day five (counted): the lending shelf, the common pot, signed credits, proven claims and others. The hosts' notices do not carry it; it reads like a day-five prompt (inferred, not checked).

Buy and Courier were read as candidate pieces for Odile Ferrant's Commission 1 (the lurker window's prompt; 084335c676f1b35f478c04c4351181bc34bcb7185b41f7f81b0a16ef683d4402); row 2's binding is the commission's point 3.
limits: Code: the research copy holds the media of dubsar only (Damgar 0.1.0, 0.1.1, Dub, Ummia 0.1.0), the Dubsar builds, the followers' build and code posted as act text. Every other app's features come from its announcements and readers' posts, not its code.
Damgar 0.2.0 to 0.2.2: their code is not in the research copy; the comparison rests on their release acts. The window folders outside _research were not read, as the brief asked.
A media hash is found where a text names it beside 'media', 'bytes' or a SHA-256; an announcement that does neither is missed. Sealed acts were not opened.
Each identity's window is the window whose kept acts hold its chain's first act; newcomers who kept none read 'unknown'.
Counts are of distinct acts across every source; a name match ('answerer', 'Courier') can include a post that only mentions it.
Until's escrow drafts appear as cMIP texts, not as an app; they are W2-B's.
